section_summary: This section comprises the second portion (pages 15–32) of the U.S. Embassy in Tokyo's monthly political report covering events in Japan during August 1940. It surveys Japan's diplomatic relations—notably heightened friction with Great Britain over reciprocal arrests and troop withdrawals from China, diplomatic and economic pressures on the Netherlands East Indies and French Indochina, border demarcation with Outer Mongolia, and rapprochement discussions with the Soviet Union—alongside ongoing military and naval operations in China. Domestically, it chronicles the Konoe Cabinet's formal proclamation of high policy and the Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere, a sweeping purge and recall of senior Foreign Service personnel, and preparations for the New National Structure (Taisei Yokusankai) movement to assist the Throne.

subfiles.about: A comprehensive monthly political review prepared by the U.S. Embassy in Tokyo surveying Japan's foreign relations, military operations in China, and domestic political transformations during August 1940.
subfiles.summary: This report reviews major international and internal developments affecting Japan during August 1940, opening with bilateral tensions with Great Britain marked by reciprocal espionage arrests, the suicide in custody of Reuters correspondent M. J. Cox, and the withdrawal of British military garrisons from Shanghai, Peiping, and Tientsin. It details Japan's southward advance diplomacy, highlighting mission negotiations with the Netherlands East Indies under Commerce Minister Kobayashi and military transit demands served on French Indochina, alongside border demarcation between Manchukuo and Outer Mongolia and efforts toward a Soviet-Japanese non-aggression pact. The despatch also summarizes Japanese air raids and anti-guerrilla operations across China, the Konoe administration's fundamental policy declaration outlining the Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere, a radical recall and restructuring of diplomatic personnel orchestrated by Vice Minister Ohashi, and the launch of the New National Structure movement to unite the nation under Imperial authority.
subfiles.title: Japan: Political Affairs, August 1940
